stories.title: 早上的一杯茶
stories.summary: A quiet start to Lin An’s day.

paragraphs.translation: This morning, Lin An got up very early. She walked to the kitchen and made herself a cup of tea.
It was raining lightly outside, but the room was peaceful. She drank tea while planning her day.

quiz.question: What was the weather like?
quiz.explanation: 窗外下着小雨 means that light rain was falling outside.

stories.title: 今天吃什么？
stories.summary: Two friends solve the daily lunch question.

paragraphs.translation: At noon, Xiao Yu and Daming were both hungry. They stood outside the office and discussed what to eat.
Xiao Yu wanted noodles, while Daming wanted rice. Then they saw a small restaurant that had both.

quiz.question: Why did the small restaurant suit both friends?
quiz.explanation: The restaurant had both foods: 两种都有。

stories.title: 坐错车了
stories.summary: A small mistake becomes a useful conversation.

paragraphs.translation: Chen Fei wanted to go to the museum, but he boarded the wrong bus. After ten minutes, the road looked unfamiliar.
He asked the driver for help. The driver smiled and told him to get off at the next stop and take bus number eight back.

quiz.question: What did the driver tell Chen Fei to do first?
options: Get off at the next stop
quiz.explanation: The driver first said 下一站下车 — get off at the next stop.

stories.title: 周末的小市场
stories.summary: Mei discovers a friendly neighbourhood market.

paragraphs.translation: Every Saturday, there is a small market near Mei’s home. Vegetables, fruit, flowers, and handmade bread are sold there.
Mei bought three red apples. The seller gave her one small pear and said, “Try this—it’s very sweet!”

quiz.question: What extra fruit did the seller give Mei?
quiz.explanation: 老板又送给她一个小梨 means the seller also gave her a small pear.

stories.title: 四个声调
stories.summary: Hear how mā, má, mǎ and mà change a word's meaning.

coach.title: Meet the four tones
notes: Pinyin uses letters to show pronunciation. The mark above the main vowel shows the tone: mā, má, mǎ, mà.
1st tone stays high and level; 2nd rises; 3rd is low (often dipping then rising when said on its own); 4th falls sharply.
Play each example separately, then repeat it. Keep the vowel sound similar and change the pitch. These are different words, not four ways to say the same word.

paragraphs.translation: Xiao An is learning pinyin. There are four characters in the book: mum, hemp, horse and scold.
The teacher says, “Listen first, then say it.” Xiao An listens again and reads slowly.

quiz.question: Which pinyin means “horse”?
quiz.explanation: 马 is mǎ, with a third-tone mark. Changing the tone can change the meaning.

stories.title: 买还是卖？
stories.summary: Practise mǎi and mài at a fruit stall.

coach.title: Third tone or fourth tone?
notes: 买 mǎi means “buy”; 卖 mài means “sell”. Their initial m and final ai match, but their tones differ.
Say mǎi low; when practising it alone, let it dip and rise. Say mài with a firm falling pitch.
Read the small mark over a: ǎ versus à. Listen, repeat, and then use the word in a sentence.

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Hello! I want to buy apples.

paragraphs.speaker: Seller
paragraphs.translation: I sell apples. How many would you like?

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: I'd like three. Thank you!

quiz.question: Which word would a customer use for “buy”?
quiz.explanation: The customer 买 mǎi (buys); the seller 卖 mài (sells).

stories.title: 四个，不是十个
stories.summary: A dumpling order helps you compare sì and shí.

coach.title: Hear s and sh
notes: 四 sì means four; 十 shí means ten. Both the initial sound and the tone change.
For s, keep your tongue near the front behind the teeth. For sh, move the tongue tip back toward the ridge behind the teeth; avoid pressing it against the palate.
Don't read pinyin like English spelling. Listen to the complete syllables sì and shí, then practise the order below.

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Hello! I'd like four steamed buns.

paragraphs.speaker: Server
paragraphs.translation: Ten?

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Four, not ten. Thank you!

quiz.question: How many buns does the customer want?
quiz.explanation: The customer corrects the order: 四个，不是十个 — four, not ten.

stories.title: 你好吗？
stories.englishTitle: A Little Question, a Light Tone
stories.summary: Meet the neutral tone in a friendly greeting.

coach.title: Keep the last syllable light
notes: 吗 ma is a question particle. Its neutral tone has no tone mark: keep it short and light, rather than giving it a fixed full tone.
In 谢谢 xièxie, the second xie is also light. Compare it with the marked first syllable.
Pinyin usually writes 你好 as nǐ hǎo. In speech, the first third tone changes to a rising tone before the next third tone. Listen for ní hǎo, while remembering the usual written form.

paragraphs.speaker: A
paragraphs.translation: Hello! How are you?

paragraphs.speaker: B
paragraphs.translation: I'm very well, thank you. And you?

paragraphs.speaker: A
paragraphs.translation: I'm well too. See you tomorrow!

quiz.question: Why does ma in nǐ hǎo ma have no tone mark?
options: It has a light neutral tone
quiz.explanation: 吗 ma is neutral-toned here: it is shorter and lighter than a full-tone syllable.

stories.title: 很高兴认识你
stories.summary: Introduce yourself and ask someone's name.

coach.title: A conversation you can reuse
notes: 我叫… means “My name is…”. Replace the example name with your own.
你叫什么名字？ asks “What's your name?”. Finish with 很高兴认识你 — “Nice to meet you”.

paragraphs.speaker: Xiao An
paragraphs.translation: Hello! My name is Xiao An. What's your name?

paragraphs.speaker: Xiao Lin
paragraphs.translation: My name is Xiao Lin. Nice to meet you!

paragraphs.speaker: Xiao An
paragraphs.translation: I'm happy to meet you too. Do you live nearby?

paragraphs.speaker: Xiao Lin
paragraphs.translation: Yes, I live nearby.

quiz.question: Which phrase introduces your name?
quiz.explanation: Use 我叫… followed by your name. 你叫什么名字？ is the question you can ask in return.

stories.title: 一杯热茶
stories.summary: Order tea, choose hot or iced, and ask the price.

coach.title: Make a simple order
notes: 我想要… means “I'd like…”. 一杯 yì bēi is “one cup”. Try changing 茶 to 咖啡.
热的还是冰的？ offers a choice: “Hot or iced?”. 多少钱？ asks “How much?”.

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Hello! I'd like a cup of tea.

paragraphs.speaker: Server
paragraphs.translation: Hot or iced?

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Hot, please. How much is it?

paragraphs.speaker: Server
paragraphs.translation: Ten yuan. Please wait a moment.

quiz.question: What does the customer order?
quiz.explanation: The customer asks for 一杯茶 (a cup of tea), then chooses 热的 (hot).

stories.title: 需要袋子吗？
stories.summary: Handle a price, a shopping bag, and payment.

coach.title: Useful checkout phrases
notes: 需要…吗？ asks “Do you need…?”. 不需要 means “don't need”.
可以…吗？ asks whether something is allowed or possible. 可以刷卡吗？ means “Can I pay by card?”.

paragraphs.speaker: Cashier
paragraphs.translation: That's twenty yuan in total. Do you need a bag?

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: No, thank you. I have a bag.

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Can I pay by card?

paragraphs.speaker: Cashier
paragraphs.translation: Yes. Thank you, goodbye!

quiz.question: Why doesn't the customer need a bag?
options: The customer has a bag already
quiz.explanation: 我有袋子 means “I have a bag”.

stories.title: 地铁站在哪里？
stories.summary: Ask where something is and follow simple directions.

coach.title: Ask, then listen for direction words
notes: 请问 is a polite way to get someone's attention before asking a question.
…在哪里？ means “Where is…?”. Listen for 一直走 (go straight), 左转 (turn left), and 右边 (on the right).

paragraphs.speaker: Visitor
paragraphs.translation: Excuse me, where is the metro station?

paragraphs.speaker: Local
paragraphs.translation: Go straight, then turn left. The station is on the right.

paragraphs.speaker: Visitor
paragraphs.translation: Is it far from here?

paragraphs.speaker: Local
paragraphs.translation: Not far. It's a five-minute walk.

quiz.question: What should the visitor do after going straight?
quiz.explanation: 然后左转 means “then turn left”. The station itself is on the right after that turn.

stories.title: 明天有空吗？
stories.summary: Invite a friend and agree on a time and place.

coach.title: Make an invitation
notes: 你明天有空吗？ asks “Are you free tomorrow?”. 一起…吧 is a friendly suggestion: “Let's… together”.
几点？ asks “What time?”. Practise changing 下午三点 to a different meeting time.

paragraphs.speaker: A
paragraphs.translation: Are you free tomorrow? Let's have tea together.

paragraphs.speaker: B
paragraphs.translation: Sure! What time?

paragraphs.speaker: A
paragraphs.translation: Three in the afternoon. Let's meet at the café.

paragraphs.speaker: B
paragraphs.translation: Okay. See you tomorrow!

quiz.question: When will the friends meet?
quiz.explanation: They are making plans for 明天 (tomorrow), at 下午三点 (3 p.m.).

stories.title: 请再说一遍
stories.summary: Keep a conversation going when you don't understand.

coach.title: A useful rescue phrase
notes: 不好意思 politely softens a request: “Excuse me / sorry”. 我没听懂 means “I didn't understand what I heard”.
请再说一遍 means “Please say it again”. 请说慢一点 asks someone to slow down. Try saying both without looking.

paragraphs.speaker: Shop assistant
paragraphs.translation: This is fifteen yuan.

paragraphs.speaker: Learner
paragraphs.translation: Sorry, I didn't understand. Please say it again.

paragraphs.speaker: Learner
paragraphs.translation: Please speak a little slower.

paragraphs.speaker: Shop assistant
paragraphs.translation: Sure. Fifteen yuan.

quiz.question: Which phrase asks someone to repeat?
options: 请再说一遍 qǐng zài shuō yí biàn
quiz.explanation: 请再说一遍 means “Please say it again”. Add 请说慢一点 if you also need a slower pace.
